follow_up_filed.title: The architectural map requirement is sited at 1-ba, where the tier is never known
follow_up_filed.why: SEC-1 / vulnerabilities[0]. This PR RETIRES the `1-ba` map requirement on the mandated path at every tier. Re-siting it at a phase where the tier is resolved is out of scope here and is written up in #61 with SecOps's 1-of-15 -> 0-of-15 measurement, its non-zero control, and the named candidate fix. Filed BEFORE this merges, per evidence.md's deferring-is-an-action rule.

spec.title: The phase-entry guard cannot tier a record at 1-ba, and cannot date one at all
spec.problem: Two QA findings from #39's Phase 4 name mutations that survived every suite, and both are the same shape: a branch of gate-phase-entry.mjs that no fixture in any suite can reach through the suite's own builders. (#43) `mk_status()` always interpolates `updated_at`, so the in-flight predicate's undatable branch -- the one that stops an undatable record from holding a project's turns open forever -- has never been exercised; mutating it to `return true` passes all 345 assertions. (#45) No fixture ever puts the `1-ba` row at a non-architectural tier, so the `tiers` column has no test; deleting it passes all 345 assertions. Both zeros RE-MEASURED at the current merge-base 2ec6dd7 with a non-zero control in the same battery (see measured_state), not inherited from the Phase 1 basis. The second finding is not only a test gap. Because commands/pipeline.md's Phase 1 **Checkpoint first:** line mandates committing `current_phase: "1-ba"` BEFORE dispatching BA (cited by QUOTED TEXT, never by line: re-derive with `git grep -n 'current_phase: "1-ba"' -- plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md`, which returns exactly one hit -- NOT `git grep -n 'Checkpoint first'`, which returns eight, one per phase, and so cannot answer the question it is asked. The Phase 1 draft of this sentence cited `:103`, which is WRONG -- `:103` at 2ec6dd7 is the risk-tiered-orchestration-depth paragraph, `:111` is 'the tier is read once after BA returns', and the mandate is at `:133` today and will move again), and `risk_tier` is BA's output, a record at `1-ba` NECESSARILY has no tier; `normalizeTier` resolves that absence to `architectural`, which switches on the architectural-only `1-ba` row and demands a `map.json` that standard-tier runs fold into Phase 1 and trivial-tier runs may skip entirely. The result is a halting control that refuses the first turn boundary of every non-architectural run, with no honest clearance route. It fired live on 2026-08-20 against this repo and was cleared by hand-seeding a tier -- a workaround, recorded as one. WHAT THE FIX COSTS, stated up front because Phase 2 found the spec had understated it: the `1-ba` row's map requirement is RETIRED on the mandated path at EVERY tier, not narrowed to the architectural one, because a row gated on a resolved tier is unreachable at the only visit where the map can still be missing. Re-siting that requirement is #61.
spec.root_cause: One root cause per issue, and they meet at the same table. (#43) The in-flight predicate's undatable branch is unreachable through `mk_status()`, which forces the `updated_at` key to exist with a well-formed value. (#45) The `tiers` column is unreachable through the fixture set, which never varies the tier at the `1-ba` row -- AND, in production, is unreachable through the WORKFLOW, because the tier does not exist at the only phase that row governs. gate-phase-entry.mjs deliberately reuses pipeline-status.mjs's staleness definition rather than inventing a second one; it did NOT reuse pipeline-status.mjs's TIER handling, and that divergence is the defect. Stated precisely, because the earlier wording of this sentence did not survive reading the code: `pipeline-status.mjs`'s `resolveTier` (scripts/pipeline-status.mjs:63-68 at origin/main 2ec6dd7) already represents an ABSENT tier as `"-"` rather than as the strictest tier; it passes a malformed one through unchanged (`if (typeof status?.risk_tier === "string") return status.risk_tier;`), so the absent/null half of this rule has a precedent in the repo and the malformed half is a NEW judgement made here.
requirements: R1. `appliesAtTier` distinguishes an UNDETERMINED risk_tier (absent, null, or any value outside KNOWN_TIERS) from a resolved one: a row carrying a `tiers` key does NOT apply when the tier is undetermined, because such a row exists at one tier precisely because its prerequisite is not producible at the others, and demanding it on a guess makes it unsatisfiable rather than strict.

R2. `normalizeTier`, `rowFor`, and the exported `satisfyingTokens` are NOT changed. The strictest-row default remains correct for `byTier` rows, where the tier is resolved by the time the row is reached; only the tiers-restricted path learns the new distinction.

R3. The undetermined-tier `not-applicable` decision carries its OWN reason wording, distinct from the resolved-tier wording (`is not a guarded phase at the <tier> tier`), so which branch fired is readable from the decision line. PROHIBITION, not a preference: that reason string MUST NOT interpolate `status.risk_tier`'s value. This is the first branch in the guard where the field is known NOT to be a KNOWN_TIERS member and has not been normalized away, which is exactly where an implementer reaches for `"${status.risk_tier}"`; the value is agent-written free text in a file that is committed and archived verbatim, nothing enforces the schema's enum at runtime, and the guard's own header already forbids this class for ask_text / events[].note / error. Acceptable wording: '.pipeline/<n> at `1-ba` carries no determined risk_tier, so a tier-restricted row does not apply.' AC2 asserts the prohibition negatively so it is falsifiable rather than aspirational.

R4. The guard's header comment states the new rule NEXT TO the existing strictest-default statement. Four things, and the first is a correction of what an earlier draft of this spec would have had Dev write: (a) the ACCURATE blast radius -- on the path pipeline.md mandates, the `1-ba` map requirement is retired at EVERY tier, surviving only for re-entry visits to `1-ba` where map.json necessarily already exists; the comment cites #61 as where it gets re-sited. It must NOT say the row does real work at the architectural tier, which is false the moment this merges and outlives the reasoning. (b) the accepted cost (a typo'd risk_tier now turns a tiers-restricted row OFF rather than ON) and why that is not contradictory: the guard already refuses to hold turns open on a record it cannot DATE, and this is the same rule for a record it cannot TIER. (c) the third instance of the same fail-open direction, free to state here because DBA measured it in the same paragraph's subject: a record the guard cannot VALIDATE as concluded is taken at its word (`completed_at` is never parsed, `final_verdict` is tested for truthiness against a closed enum), on purpose. (d) the ABSTENTION INVENTORY next to the fail-direction split, so the person who adds a fourth way to say nothing sees the first three: tooling fail-open, the mtime-tie no-subject case (8588f00), and this new undetermined-tier row-off -- of which only the third names itself in its output and is pinned by a test. (e) EVERY citation this comment makes is by QUOTED TEXT or SYMBOL plus the command that re-derives it, NEVER by line number. This is not style: the comment is permanent and AC11 pins it with a test, so a stale coordinate rots inside a defended artifact. The evidence is in this issue's own record -- the Phase 1 draft cited `pipeline.md:103` for a mandate that lives at `:133`; a knowledge-store citation of this same guard moved 241 -> 251 without anyone noticing; and one Phase 2 block cited the suite's `"deep"` token at :478 when it is at :477. Three line citations, three refs, three drifts, one issue. A symbol alone is not enough either -- it is renameable, and like a line it is READ BY NOTHING -- so the citation must carry a command a reader can RUN and get a right-or-wrong answer from -- and the command must DISCRIMINATE: `git grep -n 'Checkpoint first'` over pipeline.md returns eight hits, one per phase, which is a command that runs and answers nothing.
R5. test-gate-phase-entry.sh gains a `1-ba` x tier cell family covering {trivial, standard, architectural, undetermined}, driven through the real CLI like every other cell.

R6. test-gate-phase-entry.sh gains an `updated_at` cell family covering {absent, unparseable string, JSON null}, each paired with a fresh-`updated_at` control at the SAME phase and the SAME issue dir, so each cell discriminates rather than passing over an empty population.

R7. Every added cell asserts its FIXTURE SHAPE before gating, against the CLASS of pre-tier `not-applicable` exits rather than against one example of it. gate-phase-entry.mjs's decideForDir reaches `not-applicable` by FOUR routes before the tier check is ever evaluated -- isTerminal (any truthy `completed_at`, never parsed, so `"TBD"` counts), UNGUARDED phase, unrecognised phase, and !inFlight (any truthy `final_verdict`, including a value outside the schema's closed enum such as `"pending"`, OR undatable OR stale) -- and the last of these emits ONE reason string for three different causes. So a decision assertion alone cannot tell which route fired, and a fixture that quietly took a different route would pass. Each cell's probe asserts: `completed_at` absent-or-falsy, `final_verdict` absent-or-falsy, `current_phase` genuinely a member of GUARDED, and the intended `updated_at` / `risk_tier` shape. One line per cell, at the only moment it is free. TWO ADDITIONS at Phase 2 round 2, both narrowing what a cell may assert. (i) Every added cell asserts the DECISION (`GATE_DEC`), never the exit code alone. decideForDir has a FIFTH pre-tier exit that is NOT a `not-applicable` route and therefore does not change the four-route enumeration above: it returns `null` on an unreadable or non-object record, which the caller renders as SILENCE -- rc 0, empty stdout, empty stderr, indistinguishable from `not-applicable` to an rc-only assertion. DBA measured it on a pristine 2ec6dd7 extract with a refused control in the same loop: trailing-comma JSON, `[]`, `null` and a missing file all produced rc 0 and no output. The suite's own `gate()` helper already closes this by setting `GATE_DEC='<no-decision-on-stdout>'` when stdout is empty, so the cost is zero -- but it only helps a cell that asserts the decision. This binds hardest on R8's hand-written-body route, which is precisely where a typo'd fixture yields unparseable JSON. (ii) For the unknown-string tier cell, the probe asserts the fixture's `risk_tier` is EXACTLY the shell variable that also feeds AC2's negative assertion, which is what stops that negative assertion going vacuous if the fixture is later reworded.

R8. `mk_status()` is not modified. The cells reach their conditions through routes that already exist in this suite -- the `MK_UPDATED` env seam, `capture()`'s documented null-deletes-the-key patch, and the hand-written body AC11 already uses for exactly this problem -- and each cell carries a one-line comment naming its route, because 'add a test for the absent field' is not actionable against a builder that cannot emit one. R7's probe is load-bearing precisely for the hand-written-body route, which carries no builder guarantee about the fields in R7's class.
acceptance_criteria: AC1. `1-ba` with no `map.json` and no events decides `not-applicable` (rc 0) at BOTH `risk_tier: "trivial"` and `risk_tier: "standard"`, and `refused` (rc 2, reason naming `map.json`) at `risk_tier: "architectural"`. The three cells are asserted adjacently as one discrimination: the architectural cell is the control that proves the other two are not passing for an unrelated reason.

AC2. `1-ba` with no `map.json` and an UNDETERMINED tier decides `not-applicable` (rc 0), and the reason names the tier as undetermined rather than naming a tier the record does not carry. Asserted for all three undetermined spellings: key absent, `null`, and an unknown string. NEGATIVE HALF, which is R3's prohibition made falsifiable: for the unknown-string spelling the fixture's token is a distinctive garbage value, and the decision output is asserted NOT to contain it. Both halves are required; the positive half alone passes under an implementation that interpolates. THE TOKEN'S OWN PREMISE IS ASSERTED, because 'the output does not contain GARBAGE' passes trivially the day the fixture stops carrying GARBAGE: ONE shell variable feeds both the fixture body and the negative assertion, and R7(ii)'s probe asserts the fixture's `risk_tier` equals that variable. The token must not be a real word. Specifically NOT `"deep"`, which the suite's existing `ac11` helper already passes as its unknown-string spelling -- exactly one hit, re-derive with `git grep -n deep plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh` (it is at :477 at 2ec6dd7, not the :478 one Phase 2 block cites, which is a line citation rotting inside a single review round) -- and a negative assertion on a real word is a false failure waiting for a reword.

AC3. The `3-impl` row is UNCHANGED at an undetermined tier: with `spec.json` present and `design.json` absent, the decision is still `refused` and the reason still names `design.json`, for key-absent, `null`, and unknown-string alike. (This is the SUITE's own AC11 trio -- `suite "AC11: an unusable risk_tier resolves to the STRICTEST row, never the loosest"`, re-derive with `git grep -n 'an unusable risk_tier' plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh` -- and NOT this spec's AC11, which is a different criterion wearing the same number; see AC8 on why the added assertions must not reuse suite labels. Re-run as a regression pin: it is what proves the fix loosened the tiers column and not the strictest-row default.)

AC4. `satisfyingTokens(phase, tier)` returns byte-identical output before and after the change across the full cross product of ENTRY+EXIT x {trivial, standard, architectural, undetermined}, and the drift suite's AC18(iv)/(v) stay green. The comparison is derived by running the walk at both commits, not pinned to a count.

AC5. At `3-impl` with no `design.json`, a fresh `updated_at` decides `refused` (rc 2) and the SAME fixture with the `updated_at` key DELETED decides `not-applicable` (rc 0). Both halves are asserted; the refused half is the non-zero control that makes the not-applicable half a result.
AC6. The same paired assertion holds for `updated_at: "not-a-date"` and for `updated_at: null`.

AC7. Before each added fixture is gated, a probe asserts the fixture does not qualify for ANY of the four pre-tier `not-applicable` routes R7 enumerates other than the one the cell is testing: `completed_at` absent-or-falsy, `final_verdict` absent-or-falsy, `current_phase` in GUARDED, and the intended datability/tier shape (`Date.parse` non-finite or the key absent, for the AC5/AC6 cells; the paired control asserted datable AND under the 24h ceiling). Without this, an AC5/AC6 cell is indistinguishable from AC15(a)'s staleness cell -- byte-identical reason string -- and a hand-written body carrying a stray `final_verdict` or `completed_at` would pass while testing nothing.

AC8. Each added cell family is driven by an explicit fixture table, and the number of cells EXECUTED is counted inside the loop and asserted equal to the table's own length, so a cell that silently stops running fails instead of shrinking. The count is derived from the table, never pre-printed as a target. AND EVERY ADDED ASSERTION LABEL IS NAMESPACED `#43-...`, with the namespace asserted to have ZERO hits at the merge-base. This is not cosmetic: AC10's whole discharge is that a mutation must name a label greppable in the suite, so a fabricated label is falsifiable by grep -- and the suite ALREADY owns `suite "AC11: an unusable risk_tier resolves to the STRICTEST row"` and `suite "AC12: terminal states decline to judge"`, which are different criteria wearing this spec's new numbers. A colliding label makes AC10's grep return two unrelated sites and the control stops discriminating. Namespacing beats continuing the suite's own numbering (which runs to AC30, re-derive with `git grep -n '^suite "AC' plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh`): two OTHER open issues name this suite in their bodies -- #46 is against it directly (AC23(a)/AC28(a)) and #54 names it alongside test-status-schema-contract.sh -- so two branches both appending `AC31` re-creates this exact collision at merge time, while an issue number is unique by construction and tells the next reader which issue introduced the cell.

AC9. All three guard suites report `failed=0`, with assertion counts strictly greater than a basis DERIVED by running those same three suites at the implementation's own merge-base -- not compared against any number written in this spec. Both the derived basis and the post-change counts are recorded in impl-report.json. The two cross-suite pins in test-gate-phase-entry-hook.sh AC27 (test-stop-hook.sh and test-voice-lint.sh) must still pass at whatever values that suite holds at the merge-base; if a pin's expected value is stale the suite fails and Dev raises it rather than editing the pin to match. NO POPULATION OR COUNT IS PINNED IN THIS CRITERION: the corpus figure in measured_state is a measurement at a named ref, not a property of the repo, and it moved twice during this issue's own life.

AC10. The mutation battery is re-run at the implementation's merge-base and recorded in impl-report.json: MUT-A (`!Number.isFinite(updated)` -> `return true`), MUT-B (`Date.parse(status.updated_at ?? new Date().toISOString())`), and MUT-C (drop `tiers: ["architectural"]` from the `1-ba` row) each redden at least one NAMED assertion label that is greppable in the suite; MUT-D (`normalizeTier` default -> `trivial`) still reddens its 6 as the non-zero control, and the control is run in the SAME session as the zeros. Each mutation is applied by literal string replacement with a verified single occurrence, the changed line is printed, and the file is restored from git with `git diff --quiet` confirmed between mutations. The battery runs in a DEDICATED worktree, not the shared one (#19): Phase 2 of this very issue recorded a contamination window where one reviewer's battery corrupted another's reading.

AC11. The guard's header comment and commands/pipeline.md agree IN WRITING that the `1-ba` checkpoint necessarily precedes the tier, and the guard cites `#61` as where the retired map requirement is re-sited. ASSERTED AS A CONTENT CHECK WITH A MERGE-BASE NON-ZERO CONTROL, because the round-1 form of this criterion was SATISFIABLE BY A ZERO-LINE DIFF and its own named mutation would not have reddened it: measured at 2ec6dd7 before any change, `1-ba` occurs 5 times in the guard and 5 in pipeline.md, `risk_tier` 2 and 13, so `grep -q '1-ba' && grep -q risk_tier` passes TODAY on both files. Only `#61` (0 hits in both) was non-vacuous, and only for the guard half. DBA and SecOps found that independently and converged on one remedy; this is it, in four clauses. (a) ONE CONTIGUOUS DISTINCTIVE STRING PER FILE, not a conjunction of common tokens -- and short enough to sit on ONE line in both files, or matched with whitespace normalized, because a distinctive string long enough to span a comment's wrap point is a false failure waiting for a reflow. (b) The SAME contiguous anchor clause occurs in BOTH files: two independently chosen per-file strings cannot witness the word 'agree'. (c) The guard's occurrence is asserted WITHIN THE COMMENT BLOCK that also holds the existing strictest-default sentence (`An unusable risk_tier resolves to the STRICTEST row, never the loosest`; re-derive with `git grep -n 'STRICTEST row' plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs`), which is R4's 'NEXT TO' made mechanical -- a whole-file grep passes with the sentence pasted anywhere. The property is CO-LOCATION, not a fixed address: if Dev sites the prose in the file prologue instead, the strictest sentence moves with it and the assertion still holds. (d) impl-report.json records that EVERY half -- both files and the `#61` token -- FAILS when the same check is run against the merge-base checkout. That pre-change red is the control, measured in the same session as AC9's derived basis and recorded beside it. THE `#61` ASSERTION CARRIES ITS EXPIRY IN ITS OWN MESSAGE, substantially: 'if this fails, #61 landed or the citation moved -- re-anchor this assertion to the new siting, do not delete it', because the correct outcome for a deferral is that somebody discharges it, and an assertion whose subject can be legitimately removed must say so in its own text. WHAT THIS FIX STILL DOES NOT BIND, written down because the fix for the criterion beside it (AC9) is what introduced this defect one criterion over: a merge-base red proves the string is NEW and that the check DISCRIMINATES; it cannot prove the sentence is TRUE, and clause (b) binds a shared token, not semantic agreement. Both remain prose graded by the Phase 4 panel, and the specific thing to grade is R4(a)'s prohibition -- the comment must NOT claim the row does real work at the architectural tier.

AC12. The AC24 corpus walk's TWO anti-vacuity controls are made honest, and they must be read as a pair. Both sites are found by `git grep -n -- '-ge 4' plugins/pipeline/tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh`, which returns exactly two hits at 2ec6dd7. (a) REPLACED, the floor on `AC24_EVALUATED`: it becomes an EXACT accounting -- `AC24_EVALUATED` plus the records the loop accounted UNREADABLE equals `CORPUS_N` -- which is AC8's own derived-count idiom applied to the walk this change re-verifies. It holds by construction, and the mechanism is why: the loop's ONLY non-evaluating exit records the record by NAME (`AC24_REFUSED="$AC24_REFUSED $name(UNREADABLE)"` then `continue`), so nothing can leave the accounting silently. (b) RETAINED DELIBERATELY, the floor on `CORPUS_N` in the AC19 walk above: it is NOT converted to a derived equality, because it is (a)'s own anti-vacuity companion. `EVALUATED + UNREADABLE == CORPUS_N` is trivially TRUE at 0 == 0 + 0, and so is AC24's 'no committed record is refused' zero, so an empty population -- a broken glob, a wrong cwd, a rename of `.pipeline/` -- satisfies both without it. Nothing in the repo STATES what the corpus should contain, and inferring it from history is what evidence.md forbids, so a floor is the only available shape there. (c) That retained floor's CONSTANT drops from 4 to 1 and it gains a one-line comment naming what it is for and that it must not be finished off -- because a future reader greps `-ge 4`, finds the two sites above, and has (a)'s general argument against floors in hand. 4 is a constant taken from a population measurement over a population a DOCUMENTED operation shrinks: pipeline.md's Phase 5 sanctions removing `.pipeline/<issue>/status.json` or moving the whole dir to `.pipeline/_archived/<issue>/`, a two-level path that leaves the walk's glob entirely. `>= 1` keeps the entire anti-vacuity property (0 is the only value that makes the equality trivially true) with no false-failure mode, and a false failure in THIS suite is exactly the disarm pressure this issue exists to reduce. PREMISE CORRECTION, because this is the sentence the next reader reuses: the corpus is not 'monotonically growing', it BOTH GROWS AND IS ARCHIVED, and that makes the conclusion stronger rather than weaker -- an exact accounting is correct on both paths, while a floor decays on one and fires falsely on the other. In scope because this fix is what lets a NEW record shape -- tier-less at `1-ba` -- enter that corpus without being refused.

out_of_scope: Changing `normalizeTier`'s strictest-row default. It is correct for `byTier` rows and 6 assertions defend it; the measured MUT-D control proves they bite.
Modifying `mk_status()`. It is the input to the great majority of the suite's assertions, and all three missing conditions are reachable through routes the suite already has.

Having the guard read `spec.json`'s risk_tier as a fallback (the way pipeline-status.mjs resolveTier does). At `1-ba` spec.json does not exist either, so it solves nothing at the only phase that needs it.

RE-SITING the map requirement, which is #61. Stated accurately, because the earlier version of this entry was wrong: this change RETIRES the `1-ba` map requirement on the mandated path at EVERY tier, not just at the two where it was unsatisfiable. A row gated on a resolved tier cannot fire at the only visit where the map can still be missing; it survives only for re-entry visits to `1-ba`, when map.json necessarily already exists. SecOps measured 1-of-15 rows catching a mapless architectural run today and 0-of-15 after. What is lost is an UNDISCRIMINATING refusal -- today's row refuses trivial, standard and architectural identically at `1-ba` -- and what is gained is the removal of the disarm pressure that refusal creates. That trade is the ruling; the lost coverage is re-sited in #61, filed before this merges.

Removing the now-mostly-dead `tiers` key from the `1-ba` row, or deciding its fate. That belongs with the re-siting in #61, which must rule on it explicitly rather than leave a row that looks live and is not.
Correcting `.pipeline/43/status.json`'s operator-seeded tier in this PR (see open question q2).
The `current_phase`-absent and `events`-absent fixture gaps (see sibling_causes_considered): neither fails into a wedge, and one has no non-equivalent mutation.
Making the refusal message itself distinguish the staleness branch from the undatable branch. The cells discriminate via their paired controls and AC7's probes instead.

Validating `completed_at` as a date or `final_verdict` against status.schema.json's closed enum (DBA's nit). Both disarm rather than over-claim, which is the same fail-open direction the guard chose deliberately; R4(c) documents the direction here, and fixing it is a separate behavioural change with its own blast radius.

Phase 1's section is WRITTEN once and EXECUTED once per entry, the same way a loop body written once runs many times. Counting grep hits counts mandates, not executions. That is the whole error, and it is the one the delta's new clause names in so many words.

Re-entering Phase 1 therefore re-writes `current_phase: "1-ba"` by the general convention, with no second literal needed anywhere.
